name: Proactive decomposition for Codex beads
hypothesis: Beads assigned to Codex providers that touch 3+ files will have >50% failure rate; pre-decomposing them into 1-2 file beads will reduce Codex failure rate from ~40% to <20%
change: Add a scope check before Codex execution: if the bead's estimated file count exceeds 2, auto-decompose before first attempt rather than attempting and failing
measurement: Compare Codex failure rate in 30-iteration windows before vs after. Track iterations-to-completion for Codex beads
risk: Over-decomposition could increase overhead from bead management (more beads to track, more context switching). May slow throughput if decomposition itself fails
study_summary: Experiment declared 2026-02-17 but no implementation deployed. Metrics show no Codex-specific proactive decomposition behavior in iteration data. The 3.1% failure rate improvement (39% to 37.8%) is within noise and attributable to reactive decomposition producing well-scoped sub-beads, not the experimental change. Control limits show no anomalies. Rolling success rate at 87% is positive but driven by existing decomposition rules, not this experiment. The hypothesis remains untested.
